system.summary: Letter cipher for German: one- and two-digit numbers 2-95 with several homophones per letter (e: 18, 42, 65, 89, Sr; n: 8, 32, 49, 56, 79, m; t: 4, 28, 52, 75 ...), plus letter-like signs (a hooked long s = e, m = n, x = b, y = c and long-s ligatures); clear German between the passages; words separated by dots, commas or a slash, not by the cipher. The numbers run in a near-cycle of 24 (2, 26, 50, 73 = m; 4, 28, 52, 75 = t; 17, 41, 64, 88 = a), with a one-step slip after about 52; the order of letters within the cycle is not alphabetical, hence key_order 'random'.

prior_solution.where: The contemporary interlinear decipherment of the letter on image 57 (same writer, same file) gives the key; the bare passages of 55 and 56 carry no gloss. Not on DECODE; no edition found: Arkiv till upplysning om svenska krigens historia I-II (1854-1861, archive.org OCR) has no Chemnitz letter of 1631; a web search found none. Riksarkivet's 'Agenten Chemnitz brev till Kungl. Maj:t' (Diplomatica Germanica SE/RA/2106/F/XI/1392, 1631-1632) is not digitised and was not seen.

conditions.human_role: Daniel Bourdeau's Riksarkivet paging sweep of 13 Nov 2026 found the passages (lead 2570). Brice Dudout set the rules (protocol and key frozen by SHA-256 before one held-out measurement, thresholds fixed in advance). An AI agent transcribed, built the key, measured and wrote up. No human palaeographer checked the transcription.
models: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), agents run by Brice Dudout

solution.what: Image 57: the whole glossed letter read by eye at full resolution, 124 gloss words aligned with their cipher groups (598 letter-group pairs, gloss57_pairs.txt).
Earlier attempt (before PREREG-3, by the contributor's record): a 23-value table tried on images 55 and 56 gave 59% coverage and no reading; 55-56 were therefore not used as the test.

Key = majority letter per group from the 57 pairs only (79 values); frozen with the protocol (PREREG-3) before any group of 55, 56 or 58 was transcribed by eye. An earlier test of a 23-value table on 55+56 (coverage 59 %) had failed; 55 and 56 were therefore not reused for testing.

One measurement on the held-out page 58 left (another letter, 5 Nov 1631; 144 groups, under the 150 asked, so indicative): German letter-frequency cosine 0.969 vs 0.869 for the best of 200 permuted keys, coverage 97 %; then agreement with 58's own glosses 95.6 % of 91 letters vs 34.1 % for the best control (thresholds >= 0.85 and >= 0.30 above the best control, fixed in advance).
Images 55 and 56 transcribed by eye (452 groups) and decoded with the frozen key; read by sense; values not in the glosses restored from the sense (46=w, 29=b, 51=r, ligatures Sd=w, Sf=t) and marked.

Integration check: key rebuilt from gloss57_pairs.txt (598 pairs, 79 values) agrees with key.tsv except the restored values and 45/47; decryption of 55-56 reproduced; 58: 140/144 groups valued. Riksarkivet IIIF images 55 and 57 fetched: 68 groups of image 55 compared, 67 agree (one S2/Sf doubt); glosses of image 57 lines 1-2 agree. Strict count 68/89 = 76.4%; gaps workable, target in progress.

texts.label: Images 55 and 56: the two bare cipher passages
texts.summary: Chemnitz advises the king that the new troops at Nuremberg could harass the enemy's quarters but are too green to risk, and that the arms and guns stored at Ansbach should be seized by force before the enemy takes them, since asking the margrave's government would betray the plan to the enemy.

reading_review.by: Claude Opus 5.5 (model), agent run by Brice Dudout
reading_review.note: decryption.txt read line by line as German sentences: both passages construe throughout (unspaced, raw spelling: 'newe volck', 'travaillirens', 'ungetrewe'), normalised and translated in reading.md; 89 cipher words, 68 sure, 11 probable, 10 on values restored from the sense and marked; no human reader yet

outcome.notes: Writer identified from the signature ('M. Chemnitz') and the literature: Martin Chemnitz (1596-1645), sent by Gustav II Adolf to Nuremberg in October 1631. The glossed letter of image 57 is itself already read (the gloss), so it is not claimed.
outcome.fraction_read_source: Integration check, 13 Nov 2026, README rule (probable and restored words are holes): image 55 34/40, image 56 34/49, 68/89 = 76.4%. The contributor's figure, counting probable words, is 79/89 = 88.8%.
